slides.heading: Reconstruct Bst
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Search Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Reconstruct Bst, a medium binary search trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Rebuild a BST from its pre-order traversal (duplicates go right) using value bounds.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Rebuild a BST from its pre-order traversal (duplicates go right) using value bounds.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: In pre-order, the root comes first and everything smaller goes left, so we build with value bounds.
slides.narration: In pre-order, the root comes first and everything smaller goes left, so we build with value bounds.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Insert each value into a BST → O(n²) worst, O(n log n) average
For each node, scan for where the right subtree starts → O(n²)
Bounds recursion with a shared index → O(n)
slides.narration: Inserting each value from the root is quadratic in the worst case. Scanning for where the right subtree begins is also quadratic. Passing value bounds down and consuming the pre-order list with one shared index builds the tree in linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Each recursion accepts values within a lower and upper bound
3. Root first, then left with an upper bound, then right
slides.narration: Step by step. First, read values in order. Second, each recursion accepts values within a lower and upper bound. Third, root first, then left with an upper bound, then right.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We keep a shared index. Build returns null if the list is exhausted or the next value falls outside the current bounds. Otherwise it consumes the value, creates a node, builds the left with upper bound v, then the right with lower bound v.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Duplicates go right: use [lo, hi) bounds
Use long bounds to avoid overflow
Reset the shared index per call
slides.narration: Duplicates belong on the right, so the left bound is inclusive and the right exclusive. Use long bounds for infinity.

bullets: Explain why the index only moves forward

slides.narration: Explain that each value is consumed exactly once. Follow-ups rebuild from post-order, or a general binary tree from in-order and pre-order.
